subject: RFP: telemetry delivery and data submission protocols for misuse monitoring
messages:
From: security-ops@finsecure.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: dpa-team@finsecure.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0500
Subject: RFP question: telemetry delivery options and schema

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking our RFP. A couple of technical clarifications from our infra and security teams on the misuse-monitoring telemetry we need to ingest from Redwood in order to run investigations and automated enforcement:

1) Event types: can you enumerate the outbound event types you can deliver (e.g., generated_text, user_prompt, model_id, model_version, safety_tag, confidence_score, token_trace, moderation_result, alert_event)?
2) Delivery modes: do you support push to customer-owned S3 (cross-account), streaming webhook (with retries and signing), or a pull API? For push, what protocol, encryption and ownership model do you use?
3) Format/volume: preferred formats (JSONL, NDJSON, protobuf), compression (gz), and a sample payload schema. Typical peak TPS we might expect: 200-400 TPS during incidents — can your pipeline handle spikes?
4) Retention and export: default retention for telemetry, auto-archiving options (to customer S3), and deletion-on-demand capabilities for privacy requests.
5) PII handling: do you provide built-in redaction/pseudonymization for identifiers (email, phone, IP)? Can customers supply a salt/key for hashing user IDs?
6) Real-time alerts: can you send alert_event types with sub-second delivery guarantees? How are back-pressure and retries handled?
7) Certifications & evidence: please attach SOC 2 Type II, any pen-test summaries, and your DPA template.

Please attach a sample schema and any operational playbooks. We plan to evaluate delivery options for our EU tenants and need region-specific details (data residency + EU KMS support). If you can get back by EOD Friday that would help our scoring timeline.

Best,
Alex (security-ops@finsecure.com)
Security Operations - FinSecure

[Attachment: RFP_Schedule.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: security-ops@finsecure.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0500
Subject: Re: RFP question: telemetry delivery options and schema

Alex —

Thanks for the detailed list. Summary answers below and a couple of attachments (misuse-telemetry-spec.csv and s3_delivery_playbook.pdf). I'll also paste a compact sample JSON schema excerpt inline. Happy to walk through this on a quick call.

1) Event types (we can emit all of these; customers can opt into subsets): generated_text, user_prompt, model_id, model_version, safety_tags (array), confidence_score, token_trace (optional, sampled), moderation_result (structured), alert_event (for high-confidence misuse).

2) Delivery modes:
   - Customer-owned S3 (recommended for high-volume customers): we push NDJSON (.jsonl) files to a cross-account S3 bucket over HTTPS using TLS1.2+, server-side encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS), and we can sign uploads using an STS-assumed role you provide. File rotation is configurable (size/time).
   - Streaming webhook: HMAC-SHA256 signed POSTs. Retries use exponential backoff with durable queuing; we guarantee at-least-once delivery and include a message-id for deduplication.
   - Pull API: supported for low-volume customers; rate-limited.

3) Format/volume: NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON) is our primary format; gzipped streams supported. We support protobuf for enterprise integrations. Our pipeline supports bursty TPS — standard dedicated customers support thousands of TPS; for your stated 200-400 TPS peaks we recommend a dedicated routing policy and S3 ingestion.

4) Retention & export: default telemetry retention is 90 days for event logs used in production monitoring. Options: archived exports to your S3 (retention you control), or long-term export via periodic snapshots. We support deletion-on-demand with audit: a redaction request triggers removal and a signed audit record.

5) PII handling: built-in pseudonymization (configurable) that hashes user identifiers using an HMAC with a customer-provided salt or Redwood-managed salt (if requested). We also support pattern-based redaction (email, phone, SSN) before export. Field-level encryption is available for sensitive fields using customer KMS (AWS KMS with grants).

6) Real-time alerts: alert_event delivery can be configured as low-latency webhook push (typical 200-700ms) or a preferential S3 stream with near-real-time file roll. During back-pressure our system queues events with durable storage; webhook retries follow an exponential backoff up to 72 hours with dead-lettering.

7) Certifications & evidence: SOC 2 Type II and pen-test executive summaries are available; DPA template attached on request. See linked HubSpot record for compliance artifacts.

Sample payload (excerpt):
{
  "event_type": "generated_text",
  "timestamp": "2026-12-03T14:14:02Z",
  "model_id": "rw-text-7b-v1",
  "request_id": "req_8a7f2c",
  "user_id_hashed": "hmac:sha256:abcd...",
  "prompt_truncated": "What are the top 3 phishing techniques...",
  "generated_text": "<redacted by policy if sensitive>",
  "safety_tags": ["policy:phishing"],
  "confidence_score": 0.92
}

Action items:
- We attached misuse-telemetry-spec.csv (full field list) and s3_delivery_playbook.pdf.
- Can you confirm preferred delivery mode (S3 vs webhook) and provide expected peak TPS by Tue 7 Dec?
- Would you like us to schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough next week?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: misuse-telemetry-spec.csv (text/csv), s3_delivery_playbook.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: security-ops@finsecure.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: dpa-team@finsecure.com
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: RFP question: telemetry delivery options and schema

Rafael —

Thanks for the thorough reply and the attachments — we reviewed the spec. A few follow-ups from infra and privacy:

- Webhook signing: can you share details on the HMAC timestamp window and how replay attacks are prevented? Is there nonce support or strict timestamp tolerance?
- Delivery guarantees: you mentioned at-least-once; what deduplication mechanism do you provide? Is there a message-id header?
- GDPR & residency: we need EU-region-only storage for telemetry from EU tenants and support for customer-managed KMS in eu-west-1. You listed region: can you confirm data never leaves EU for those tenants?
- PII & deletions: for deletions, will you provide a deletion certificate (signed) and a timeline SLA?
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II, pen-test summary, and your sample DPA — can you deliver PDFs for our procurement folder?

Also, for alert_event: do you support a separate low-latency lane (pre-filtered) that only sends alerts to the webhook and not the full telemetry stream? That would help our incident playbooks.

If you can include the webhook sample headers and a short example of a signed payload that will address replay protection, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Security Operations - FinSecure

[Attachment: internal_scoring_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: security-ops@finsecure.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 10:09:00 -0500
Subject: Re: RFP question: telemetry delivery options and schema

Alex —

Great questions. Short answers and links to artifacts below; happy to set up a 30-minute technical call next week with our infra leads (I can include Monica from Product Ops and Marissa from Safety Engineering).

Webhook signing/replay protection:
- We sign each webhook with HMAC-SHA256 using a per-customer secret. Each message includes: X-RW-Timestamp (ISO8601), X-RW-Message-Id (UUID), and X-RW-Signature (hex of HMAC). The receiver should verify signature over the concatenation of timestamp + message-id + body. We recommend a ±5 minute tolerance window; we include monotonic message-ids for ordering.

Deduplication and delivery guarantees:
- Message-Id is a stable UUID per event. We implement at-least-once delivery with X-RW-Message-Id; your endpoint can dedupe on that id. We also provide a delivery-report API so you can reconcile receipts and processing state.

EU residency & KMS:
- EU region support: yes — telemetry for EU tenants can be routed to eu-west-1 and stored in customer S3 in eu-west-1. We will not replicate EU-tenant telemetry to other regions unless explicitly enabled. Customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) is supported in eu-west-1 for field-level encryption.

Deletion SLA & certificate:
- Deletion requests: standard SLA is 72 hours for indexed telemetry and 7 days for cold archive; we emit a signed deletion certificate (SHA256 hash of the deleted object keys + timestamp + signer) for audit.

Low-latency alert lane:
- Yes. We support a filtered alert_event lane that pushes only alert_event objects to your webhook with sub-second median latency. Full telemetry continues to flow to S3 for forensic analysis.

Artifacts delivered (attached to this message):
- SOC_2_Type_II_redacted.pdf (exec summary) [available under NDA for full report]
- pen_test_summary_2026.pdf
- DPA_template_finsecure_draft.docx
- s3_delivery_playbook.pdf (operational steps and example bucket policies)

Next steps:
- Please confirm preferred delivery mode and provide an expected TPS profile (normal and peak) so we can size a dedicated feed.
- If agreeable, I'll schedule a 30-min call with Product Ops and Safety Engineering (Monica/Marissa) for next Tue/Wed.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
